title: Familie, met een beetje -je
summary: Family words and your first diminutive (-je) as warmth

blocks.title: Wie is wie
blocks.body: Meet the family: *moeder* (mother), *vader* (father), *broer* (brother), *zus* (sister), *opa* (grandpa), *oma* (grandma), *partner* (partner), *kind* (child). All simple, all worth knowing cold.

blocks.title: -je: the sound of warmth
blocks.body: Add **-je** to a noun and it shrinks — but for siblings, it usually just means *love*, not size: *broer* → *broertje*, *zus* → *zusje*. Dutch people call an older sibling *broertje/zusje* their whole life — the size doesn't matter, the warmth does.
blocks.callout: **Diminutives are always *het*** — no exceptions, even when the original word is a de-word.

pairs.right: het broertje — the little brother / bro
pairs.note: Diminutives are always *het*, even though *broer* itself is a de-word.

pairs.right: het zusje — the little sister / sis
pairs.note: Same shift: *zus* is de, *zusje* is always het.

blocks.explain: Diminutives (-je) are always *het*, no exceptions — even for de-words like *zus*.

blocks.prompt: Type the warm Dutch word for 'little brother' (or just 'bro').
blocks.hint: broer ends in r after a long vowel sound — add -tje.
blocks.explain: *broertje* — after l/n/r preceded by a long vowel or diphthong, the diminutive is -tje, not just -je.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.
Introduce a family member the warm way.

blocks.scene: Emma shows you a photo on her phone.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.nl: Kijk, dit is mijn moeder en mijn vader.
lines.en: Look, this is my mother and my father.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Wat leuk! En wie is dit?
lines.en: How nice! And who is this?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.spotlight: zusje — the diminutive makes it warm, not literally small.

lines.speaker: You
lines.en: Do you also have a brother?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.nl: Ja, mijn broertje Tim — hij is eigenlijk ouder dan ik, hoor!
lines.en: Yes, my little bro Tim — he's actually older than me!
lines.spotlight: broertje — still 'little brother' even though he's older. It's affection, not age.

questions.q: Why does Emma call Tim her 'broertje' even though he's older than her?

blocks.prompt: Introduce your family in Dutch. Use at least one diminutive (broertje/zusje) for warmth.
